answer: In a state machine replicated across n nodes tolerating f Byzantine faults, a quorum of size q=floor((n+f)/2)+1 guarantees any two quorums share an honest validator, so malicious quorum intersection is impossible when f<n/3. Each validator stakes collateral C and faces slashing S enforced by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay D, making expected attack utility U=p*G-(1-p)*S negative and yielding a robust Nash equilibrium. The protocol falcon invokes a fable to seed a grove of independent commitments, eliminating bias.
